name: EAAA India Alternatives Ltd
title: EAAA India Alternatives Ltd - 545008 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Alternatives asset manager reports H1 FY27 PAT of INR169 crore (+35% YoY) on fee-paying AUM of INR49,164 crore, with fundraising of about INR20,000 crore in H1 and dry powder of INR20,000-25,000 crore, but no supply-side or capacity content.

summary.headline: H1 FY27 PAT rose 35% YoY to INR169 crore; fee-paying AUM reached INR49,164 crore, up 23% on a 3-year CAGR.
summary.overview: First earnings call after the company's recent listing, covering Q2 and H1 FY27 (period ended 30 September 2026). Total income for H1 was INR616 crore (up 35% YoY) and management and advisory fee was INR333 crore (up 24% YoY). Q2 PAT was INR88 crore (up 28% YoY, up 9% QoQ), with PAT yield stable at about 0.71-0.72% of fee-paying AUM. Management guided to 20-30% medium-term growth in fee-paying AUM and PAT, and said the Q1 figures included the full exit of Infrastructure Fund 1, which affected income and expenses.

financial_highlights.change: 23% 3-year rolling CAGR; 28% YoY from about INR38,500 crore
up from about 25% a year ago

financial_highlights.value: about INR95,000 crore (including dry powder and commitments)
INR7 per share (140% of face value)

segments.name: Fundraising
segments.commentary: Raised about INR8,250 crore across special situations, infrastructure and private equity funds in H1 FY27, plus about INR12,000 crore in listed InvIT strategies, totalling close to INR20,000 crore in H1.

segments.name: Deployment and realisations
segments.commentary: Won the TOT-19 bundle under the National Monetisation Plan at INR2,259 crore (about 600 lane km, Tamil Nadu), and acquired a 95% occupied Grade A office park in Pune of about 1 million sq ft. Collected upwards of INR6,300 crore of realisations across strategies.

segments.name: Own-and-operate assets
segments.commentary: Owns and operates about 5.6 million sq ft of completed office space, about 7,700 km of roads, 1.73 GW of solar and about 1,800 circuit km of transmission lines.

segments.name: Credit
segments.commentary: Over 17 years, invested about INR43,000 crore across 190+ companies and realised more than INR46,000 crore. Growth capital given to Cyient Semiconductors, Gujarat Themis and Great White.

guidance_outlook: Medium to long-term growth of 20-30% in fee-paying AUM and PAT.
Aspirational PAT yield of 65-70 basis points on fee-paying AUM.
VAR (variable/carry) PAT expected at 25-30% of overall PAT, now spread across 7 funds and 5 strategies.
Aspiration to distribute about 40-50% of profits; long-term dividend payout of around 50% of annual earnings is under consideration, and management invited views on it.

Special Situations Fund, Infrastructure Yield Fund and second vintage of Commercial Real Estate Fund are in fundraising over the next few quarters; Private Equity Fund 2 expected to be nearly 3x Fund 1.
capex_capacity: Dry powder within AUM estimated at INR20,000-25,000 crore; finance team to provide exact figure.
Over FY26 and H1 FY27, about INR31,000 crore raised, of which about INR11,000 crore is listed InvIT capital and about INR20,000 crore is fund capital, mostly available as dry powder.
Infrastructure Fund 1 fully exited in H1 FY27 (gross IRR about 19.3%).
Recent acquisitions: TOT-19 road assets (INR2,259 crore) and the Pune office park (about 1 million sq ft).
demand_pricing: Distribution cost averages about 30 bps of AUM; with a 50:50 institutional-to-HNI mix, P&L distribution cost is about 60 bps. Amortised over 6-7 years, this is about 3.5-4% of distribution cost. Cash payment is 1/3 upfront and 2/3 over the fund's trail period.

Institutional clients (about 49% of AUM) are approached directly; HNI, UHNI and family office clients (about 51%) come through distributors. Management said there is no VAR sharing with distributors. Distributor concentration was not disclosed.
About 77% of AUM comes from repeat clients; 5,750+ unique client relationships.
Management fee grew 23% YoY versus FPAUM growth of 28%, because the Infrastructure Fund 1 exit reduced fee-paying AUM and new capital accrues over several quarters.

qa_highlights.question: How visible is VAR (variable carry) in income and yield strategies versus PE/VC, and is the book's visibility high?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said visibility is fairly high: hurdle returns do not compound because annual cash flows are paid out, the strategies are non-equity correlated, and owned assets have about 20-year contracted cash flows. Slide 14 was cited.

qa_highlights.question: What is the distribution mix (direct versus external distributors), and what is the overall AUM including commitments?
qa_highlights.answer: Institutions are direct and HNI/family offices go through distributors. Total AUM is about INR95,000 crore, including dry powder that will later convert to fee-paying AUM.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the deferred distribution cost amortised in Q1?
qa_highlights.answer: Infrastructure Fund 1 was exited ahead of its scheduled life, so the remaining forward-period distribution cost was expensed in Q1. There is no VAR sharing with distributors.

qa_highlights.question: What is the difference in yield and unit economics between real assets and credit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said real assets are lower-beta with lower gross yields, but the funds target similar unit economics, measured net of distribution costs (Slide 15). Infrastructure Fund 1 delivered a gross IRR of about 19.3%.

qa_highlights.question: How is carry realised, and when is it paid?
qa_highlights.answer: Carry is paid after client hurdle returns are met. Because many hurdles are paid annually, carry is more certain and gets realised over time across vintages (Slide 42 illustrates this).

qa_highlights.question: What is the dry powder mix and planned fund launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Special Situations, Infrastructure Yield and CRE Fund 2 are in fundraising over the next few quarters, and PE Fund 2 is expected to be about 3x Fund 1. A breakup of the INR20,000 crore raised was promised separately.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management fee growth lower than FPAUM growth, and how does AUM convert to FPAUM?
qa_highlights.answer: Fees are calculated on daily FPAUM, so new raises flow through over several quarters, and the Infrastructure Fund 1 exit reduced the base. The AUM-to-FPAUM gap reflects repaid capital and dry powder, which is about INR20,000-25,000 crore.

risks_watch: Management fee growth (23%) trails FPAUM growth (28%) in the short term; watch whether the gap narrows as new raises get deployed.
Q1 included one-off items from the Infrastructure Fund 1 exit (distribution cost expensed early), so the quarterly run-rate needs to be read with care.
VAR concentration and timing: carry depends on hurdle returns and realisations, and the VAR share target is 25-30% of PAT.
Dry powder of about INR20,000-25,000 crore must be deployed to convert into fee-paying AUM; the detailed breakup was pending.
Distributor concentration (top three or five) was not disclosed.
Dividend payout policy (around 50% long-term) is still open for shareholder views.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, fundraising and the 3-year FPAUM CAGR. More cautious and deferential on specifics: several questions on distribution cost cash flows, fee-to-FPAUM translation and fund-level breakups were deferred to the finance team.
key_quotes: We have grown, as I said earlier, at a 23% CAGR on a 3-year rolling basis, and which is what is also the number for 30th September 2026.

We are a standalone pure-play alternative asset manager on the income and yield side, and therefore there is no conflict with any distributor in terms of distribution of these products domestically and globally.
We have decided to keep this capability in-house even though in the short term it might look costlier, but we do believe that in the long term this is a significant strategic advantage for us.

growth.why: Management guides 20-30% medium-to-long-term growth in fee-paying AUM and PAT, backed by about INR20,000 crore H1 fundraising, INR20,000-25,000 crore dry powder and funds in fundraising (Special Situations, Infrastructure Yield, CRE Fund 2, PE Fund 2 about 3x Fund 1), but no dated capacity additions or quantified timelines.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: PAT yield is stable at about 0.71-0.72% of FPAUM against a 65-70 bps aspiration, and cost-to-income is steady at 64-65%, so margin uplift depends on mix and carry rather than guided cost actions.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No dated capacity additions were given; the call covered fund fundraising and acquired assets (TOT-19 roads INR2,259 crore, Pune office park about 1 million sq ft) rather than new capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FPAUM grew 28% YoY to INR49,164 crore and about INR20,000 crore was raised in H1, with INR20,000-25,000 crore of dry powder to deploy, supporting 20-30% medium-term growth guidance.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed; the asset-light fund model with dry powder of INR20,000-25,000 crore means no utilisation-driven capex trigger was stated.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided 20-30% medium-to-long-term growth in FPAUM and PAT, with H1 PAT up 35% and Q2 PAT up 28% YoY, but the guidance is new and no interim upgrade was signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Management fee grew only 23% against FPAUM growth of 28%, and the dry powder breakup was deferred, so fee conversion could lag the 20-30% guide if deployment slows.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Special Situations Fund, Infrastructure Yield Fund and CRE Fund 2 are in fundraising over the next few quarters, and PE Fund 2 is expected to be about 3x Fund 1.

rows.label: Dry powder deployment into fee-paying AUM
rows.why: About INR20,000-25,000 crore of dry powder within AUM will convert to FPAUM as it is deployed, though the exact breakup is pending.

rows.label: Dividend payout policy change to about 50%
rows.why: Long-term payout of around 50% is under consideration and views were invited, versus a current INR7 per share dividend and an aspiration of 40-50% distribution.

rows.label: VAR (carry) PAT contribution at 25-30%
rows.why: VAR is expected at 25-30% of PAT, spread across 7 funds and 5 strategies, and carry is more certain as hurdles are paid annually, though timing depends on realisations.

tone.note: Management was confident on 20-30% FPAUM and PAT growth, the 3-year CAGR and fundraising of about INR20,000 crore in H1, but deferred on distribution cash flows, fee-to-FPAUM translation and fund-level breakups; analysts probed VAR visibility and the reasons for the lower management fee growth.
